::: {.research-page}

<div class="research-intro">
<p>
My research focuses on statistical methodology, optimal experimental design,
computational statistics, optimization, and machine learning. I am particularly
interested in developing computational methods for complex statistical
problems, including multi-objective design optimization and robust statistical
modeling.
</p>
</div>


::: {.research-grid}


<!-- ====================================================== -->
<!-- 01 OPTIMAL EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN -->
<!-- ====================================================== -->

::: {.research-card}

<div class="research-number">01</div>

<div class="research-title">
Optimal Experimental Design
</div>

<div class="research-description">
My research in optimal experimental design focuses on constructing efficient designs for statistical modeling and scientific experimentation. It considers multiple design objectives, computational optimization, and the trade-offs that arise when different statistical criteria must be satisfied simultaneously. This work aims to make optimal design methods more flexible and computationally practical for complex experimental settings.
</div>

<div class="research-tags">
<span>Optimal Design</span>
<span>Multi-objective Optimization</span>
<span>Pareto Front</span>
</div>

<div class="research-toggle" onclick="toggleResearch(this)">
<span class="research-arrow">▶</span>
<span class="research-toggle-text">View related publication</span>
</div>

<div class="research-expanded">

<div class="research-pub-title">
Multi-Objective Optimal Experimental Design
</div>

<div class="research-section-intro">
This work develops particle-swarm-based optimization methods for constructing
Pareto-optimal experimental designs under multiple competing criteria,
including I-, G-, and D-optimality. The goal is to efficiently characterize
trade-offs among different design objectives and provide a collection of
candidate designs rather than a single optimal solution.
</div>



<div class="research-pub-title">
Input-Response Experimental Design
</div>

<div class="research-publication">

<strong>Yang, X.</strong>, Lu, L., & Anderson-Cook, C. M. (2024).
Input-response space-filling designs incorporating response uncertainty.
<em>Statistical Analysis and Data Mining: The ASA Data Science Journal</em>,
17(1), e11648.
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1002/sam.11648"
   target="_blank">DOI</a>

<div class="paper-note">
Develops an input-response space-filling design framework that incorporates
response uncertainty, allowing the design to account for coverage in both
the experimental input space and the resulting response space.
</div>

</div>

</div>

:::


<!-- ====================================================== -->
<!-- 02 SEQUENTIAL EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN -->
<!-- ====================================================== -->

::: {.research-card}

<div class="research-number">02</div>

<div class="research-title">
Sequential Experimental Design
</div>

<div class="research-description">
My research in sequential experimental design focuses on efficient data collection when experiments can be conducted and updated over multiple stages. It includes space-filling design, adaptive selection of new experimental points, and design augmentation based on information already collected. These methods are particularly useful for exploring complex design spaces while controlling experimental cost and improving the information obtained from each stage.
</div>

<div class="research-tags">
<span>Sequential Design</span>
<span>Space-Filling Design</span>
<span>Adaptive Design</span>
<span>Design Augmentation</span>
</div>

<div class="research-pub-title">
Space-Filling Design Methodology
</div>


<div class="research-publication">
<strong>Yang, X.</strong>, Lu, L., & Anderson-Cook, C. M. (2026).
Quick Input-Response Space-Filling (QIRSF) Designs.
<em>Quality and Reliability Engineering International</em>.
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1002/qre.70062" target="_blank">DOI</a>

<div class="paper-note">

<div class="research-publication">
<strong>Yang, X.</strong>, Lu, L., & Anderson-Cook, C. M. (2025).

<a href="https://doi.org/10.1080/00224065.2025.2513504" target="_blank">DOI</a>

<div class="paper-note">
Develops a scalable method for non-uniform space-filling designs that allows
experimental points to be concentrated in regions requiring greater attention.
</div>
</div>


<div class="research-publication">
<strong>Yang, X.</strong>, Lu, L., & Anderson-Cook, C. M. (2024).
Input-response space-filling designs incorporating response uncertainty.
<em>Statistical Analysis and Data Mining: The ASA Data Science Journal</em>,

<a href="https://doi.org/10.1002/sam.11648" target="_blank">DOI</a>

<div class="paper-note">

<div class="research-number">03</div>

<div class="research-title">
Statistical Methodology & Applications
</div>

<div class="research-description">
My research in statistical methodology connects statistical modeling with real-world data analysis. It includes regression and longitudinal methods, statistical inference, and data-driven approaches for understanding complex relationships in observational data. Applications have covered transportation, mobility, travel behavior, equity, resilience, and other social and behavioral problems, demonstrating how statistical methods can support both scientific understanding and practical decision-making.
</div>

::: {.research-card}

<div class="research-number">04</div>

<div class="research-title">
Computational Statistics & Machine Learning
</div>

<div class="research-description">
My research in computational statistics and machine learning combines statistical methodology with modern computational tools for analyzing complex data. It includes robust statistical modeling, optimization, interpretable machine learning, survival analysis, and neural-network methods. A central interest is understanding not only predictive performance, but also model robustness and interpretation, with applications ranging from behavioral and transportation data to biomedical and health-related classification problems.
</div>

<div class="research-tags">
<span>Machine Learning</span>
<span>Robust Modeling</span>
<span>Interpretable AI</span>
<span>Scientific Computing</span>
</div>

<div class="research-toggle" onclick="toggleResearch(this)">
<span class="research-arrow">▶</span>
<span class="research-toggle-text">View related research & publications</span>
</div>


<div class="research-expanded">


<div class="research-pub-title">
Robust Logistic Modeling and Neural Networks
</div>

<div class="research-section-intro">
This work compares conventional likelihood and cross-entropy approaches with
alternative distance-based estimation methods. The methods are evaluated
through simulation studies and real-world classification problems, including
biomedical and health-related data, with attention to robustness, predictive
performance, and computational implementation.
</div>


<div class="research-pub-title">
Machine Learning Applications
</div>

<script>
function toggleResearch(button) {

  const content = button.nextElementSibling;
  const arrow = button.querySelector(".research-arrow");
  const text = button.querySelector(".research-toggle-text");

  const isOpen = content.classList.contains("research-expanded-open");

  if (isOpen) {

    content.classList.remove("research-expanded-open");
    arrow.textContent = "▶";

  } else {

    content.classList.add("research-expanded-open");
    arrow.textContent = "▼";

  }
}
</script>
